QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_26

question.text: Under SAS-400 the Workplace Gender-Wage-Gap indicator is computed as:

answer.text: Female median wage / Male median wage × 100
(Male median wage − Female median wage) / Male median wage × 100

explanation.text: The Logic: The standard gender wage gap formula is (Male median wage − Female median wage) / Male median wage × 100. A gap of zero means parity; a positive gap means women earn less than men. This is the conventional ILO/OECD-aligned formulation used for wage-gap disclosure. The Trap: Option B expresses Female/Male as a ratio (a related but distinct inverse measure, not a gap). Option C is just headcount, not a wage measure. Option A is average payroll, not a gender comparison. Note: The cited SIA workbook chapter identifies SAS-400 as the gender-equality standard and presents the Sakhi healthcare case, but it does not contain the specific wage-gap formula. The framing above reflects general industry/regulatory practice rather than a workbook-page citation.
